title: It’s an Usaunny, Desu-pyon
text: “Aiming Lancer X! Brionac X! Gungnir X! Liberation Faa-ai X! Liberation Firestorm X! Liberation Prominence X! Hahaha! Weak! You’re all far too weak!”
“““Wooo! Yah!”””

I’d dashed off for a spirited round of hunting deep in the mountains near Siltvelt, I say. Rabbit Guy’s stats had been analyzed as running a little low, after all. Best to boost them up while I had the chance. Crocodile Guy had looked rather envious ever since becoming Crocodile Guy, and a stat boost does wonders for one’s confidence, indeed.
“I—I’d heard stories, but this is outright slaughter—gyaaaaaaah!”

Rabbit Guy really does make a racket. He’s used to riding on a Filolial-sama’s back, and yet here he was screaming his head off. Making a face like that hardly makes for convincing rabbit cuteness. We took a break partway through the hunt.

“Now then, Rabbit Guy. You ought to study the kind of look that gets you doted on by Father. A clumsy attempt to curry favor will be seen through immediately. You must gaze up with eyes shining, as if silently pleading, ‘Won’t you pet me, from the bottom of your heart?’”

Of course, one must never approach Father with strange ulterior motives. It’s best to be petted with a pure heart. Otherwise Father quietly puts some distance between you—I know this from experience. You must approach with such sincerity that not even a Filolial-sama herself would suspect a thing.
“Haah… haah… I’m having trouble understanding… what exactly you’re trying to teach me here.”
“How to get Father to pet you, I say. And also, hurry up and trust me. Otherwise I can’t apply the enhancement, and you’ll get kicked and it’ll hurt.”
“Please stop assigning me such bizarre roles!”

Above all, the performance had to be convincing enough to slip past even Filo-tan’s watchful eyes. And who better suited to the task than Rabbit Guy, who delivers such gripping performances at the circus every single time? He would see it through properly, indeed. Precisely because I myself have become an Usaunny, I simply cannot allow Rabbit Guy to phone in a half-hearted performance. Standing in for me demands nothing less than perfection, I say.
“Such an impossible demand…”
“Hurry it up, I say.”
And so, until the sun went down, I continued reinforcing Rabbit Guy’s stats while also coaching his acting for the day that was surely coming.
“Ugh… I’m exhausted.”
The moment we got back, Rabbit Guy collapsed straight onto his assigned bed at the circus.
“Sounds like it was quite the brutal training.”
Crocodile Guy, it seemed, had already returned.
“The content itself… was just clinging to the back of a Filolial as it darted around at high speed, but… I was made to perform this weirdly mocking laugh over and over until he was satisfied… ugh.”
“Ahh…”
“Well then, that ought to do for the boost. I daresay you’ve toughened up a bit.”
“If I got that much out of it in a single day… I suppose that counts as a bargain.”
“Not that I’m happy about it in the slightest.”

I heard some grumbling from Rabbit Guy, but I chose not to notice. In any case, the groundwork was largely complete now. By tomorrow, it would be about time for Filo-tan to hatch. Having to suppress my urge to rush and see Father was, admittedly, rather painful. I couldn’t help but worry—was he properly following the instructions I’d left him, was he being pestered by strange sorts, and so on. Having provoked Trash, this was indeed a source of concern. But this was Father we were talking about. Should anything truly abnormal occur, surely he would find a way to reach me. Even thinking that, though, simply going to sleep like this just wouldn’t sit right with me. Ah, that’s right. Time to put my decided plan into action. Now then, Itsuki… you’ve been quite the nuisance for quite some time, so let’s make sure you get your due.
“Hahaha, well then, Rabbit Guy, do rest up nicely. Farewell for now, I say.”
“Sounds like he’s off somewhere again.”
“Should we stop him…? No, honestly, all that guy ever does is wander off somewhere or play with the Filolials until he passes out.”
And with that, I set off once more.
No, that’s not quite right—time to commence operations, pyon!

At a certain inn. I’d gone poking around the taverns of the town I’d marked, and sure enough, found the Smoked Meats living it up in a raucous party. Apparently they were holding a banquet under the guise of “restoring their spirits” with their reward money.
“Itsuki-sama, thanks to you once again today, we were able to teach evil the meaning of justice!”
“Indeed! I’m sure they’ll repent after this.”
“And this means more slaves of the kingdom will be saved as well!”
The Smoked Meats, drinks in hand, seemed to be flattering Itsuki in a desperate bid to avoid losing their standing in the pecking order.
“I suppose so. But if we don’t work even harder, evil will never truly vanish, will it…”

Itsuki looked deep in thought, though his expression suggested he wasn’t really thinking much of anything at all. And where Itsuki couldn’t see, the Smoked Meats wore expressions vile enough to induce vomiting. Their true feelings were written plainly on their faces—the unmistakable look of “what’s the point of saving slaves, anyway.”
“Itsuki-sama, apparently there’s a circus out there kidnapping people. We simply must investigate!”
“…That would be Naofumi-san’s group, I imagine. Since they seem quite skilled at hiding evidence and never get caught, we’ll need to do our groundwork thoroughly.”
Was Itsuki really going to come inspect the circus we put on every single time? Please, spare me.
“In any case… I think I’ll head back to my room and rest now.”

Itsuki cut the celebration with his companions short and headed back toward his room at the inn. This was my chance. Making sure not to be noticed by Itsuki, I used Fireflasher to quietly dispose of whoever was keeping watch, then followed after him.
Itsuki strode briskly to his assigned room at the inn and unlocked the door. With a creak, the door swung open, and light from the hallway spilled into the dark room. Just as Itsuki stepped inside—
“—?! Who’s there!”
The moment the light spilled in, Itsuki noticed someone else in the room and let out a cry.
“Pardon the late-night intrusion—”

If I said “I say” there, it would give me away, wouldn’t it. I took a step forward and revealed myself. My form was covered entirely in fur, with long, perky ears—an adorable little creature indeed. And to top it off, wearing a Santa hat… a full-on fluffy Usaunny getup. Yes, I had used Fairy Morph to change my appearance and come to see Itsuki. Ah, my thoughts were wandering. If I said “I say” as usual, there was every chance Itsuki would see through my disguise. I’d come here specifically to give Itsuki a proper scolding, so I needed to keep the act convincing enough not to get caught. Which meant, in the spirit of playing an Usaunny character, I needed a new verbal tic.
“Desu-pyon.”
Right, “I say” simply wouldn’t do—“Desu-pyon” was much better.
“Nice to meet you, desu-pyon. My name is Usaunny Desu-pyon.”
“I—is that so…”
Itsuki checked my appearance several times before responding.
“What exactly is going on here. This is my room, you know?”
“That’s correct, desu-pyon. By the way, would you happen to be Itsuki Kawasumi, the Bow Hero, desu-pyon?”
It was a rather brazen question, but a necessary introduction nonetheless. So even though I already knew the answer, I asked Itsuki anyway.
“…No, that’s not right.”

Ah, so he was going to deny his identity even here. As I recalled, Itsuki’s stance was that he didn’t casually broadcast his position as a Hero, keeping it hidden instead. Something about how being recognized made it that much harder to carry out his righteous activities—a rather bothersome philosophy, if you ask me.
“Lying is no good, desu-pyon. Well, whether Itsuki Kawasumi is hiding his true identity or not makes no difference to me, desu-pyon. I’ve already done my research on that front, desu-pyon.”
“Just who are you.”
“Me, pyon? I’m Usaunny Desu-pyon!”
“I already heard that part. What I’m asking is why exactly this ‘Usaunny’ has broken into my room!”
That part had been easy enough—I’d simply phased through the wall and gotten there ahead of time.
